studies.Reference: Soy, isoflavones, and breast cancer risk in Japan.
studies.Authors: Yamamoto S, Sobue T, Kobayashi M, Sasaki S, Tsugane S,
studies.Journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: The frequency of soy consumption, including miso soup, was assessed using a self-administered questionnaire.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 21 852 Japanese female residents (aged 40-59 years) from four public health center areas completed a self-administered questionnaire.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The adjusted RRs for breast cancer for women in the highest quartile were 0.46 (95% CI = 0.25 to 0.84).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Consumption of miso soup and isoflavones was inversely associated with the risk of breast cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: 179 women were diagnosed with breast cancer during the follow-up period.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Consumption of miso soup and isoflavones was assessed using a self-administered questionnaire.

studies.Reference: Soya foods and breast cancer risk: a prospective study in Hiroshima and Nagasaki, Japan.
studies.Authors: Key TJ, Sharp GB, Appleby PN, Beral V, Goodman MT, Soda M, Mabuchi K
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Women completed dietary questionnaires in 1969-1970 and/or in 1979-1981.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: The association between soya foods and breast cancer risk was investigated in a prospective study of 34759 women.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: for miso soup, relative risks were 1.03 (0.81-1.31) for consumption two to four times per week and 0.87 (0.68-1.12) for consumption five or more times per week.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: The risk for breast cancer was not significantly associated with consumption of soya foods.
extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: for miso soup, relative risks were 1.03 (0.81-1.31) for consumption two to four times per week and 0.87 (0.68-1.12) for consumption five or more times per week.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Women were followed for incident breast cancer until 1993.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: for miso soup, relative risks were 1.03 (0.81-1.31) for consumption two to four times per week and 0.87 (0.68-1.12) for consumption five or more times per week, relative to consumption once a week or less.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Insufficient studies to perform formal publication bias testing.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an effect size of 0.67 (95% CI: 0.36–1.24), indicating no statistically significant association between miso and breast cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by substantial heterogeneity (I² = 72.47%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.
